title: Achieve near-complete plaque psoriasis clearance through IL-17 blockade

concept.text: Produce near-complete skin clearance in a large proportion of people with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis through targeted biologic treatment. This is disease control during treatment, rather than permanent immune tolerance. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by randomized trials meeting PASI75 and clear/almost-clear investigator endpoints, with at least half of treated patients achieving PASI90 at week 12. Test set by: FDA sets approval; pivotal investigators prespecified the psoriasis endpoints. The majority-PASI90 boundary is an editorial criterion, not an FDA licensing minimum. Reported achieved: FDA approved secukinumab (Cosentyx) on 21 January 2015; the 300 mg groups achieved PASI90 in 59% and 54% in two pivotal trials. Overlaps: DER-03, IMM-04. Sources given: [FDA Cosentyx original approval package](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2015/125504Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [Cosentyx prescribing information and PASI outcomes](https://www.dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=77c4b13e-7df3-42d4-81db-3d0cddb7f67a&type=display).

page.title: IL-17 blockade for plaque psoriasis
page.definition: A licensed biologic blocks signalling by interleukin-17 (IL-17), a family of inflammatory proteins, in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. Some recipients achieve PASI90 during treatment: at least a 90% reduction in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index, which combines affected skin area, redness, thickness and scaling.

goal.need: For all forms of psoriasis, WHO estimated approximately 100 million people affected worldwide in 2016. The secukinumab registration-trial population documents remaining skin disease and previous treatment failures, providing a population in which to test another mechanism of disease control.

figures.caption: Baseline characteristics in four placebo-controlled secukinumab trials
figures.note: These figures describe trial participants with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, rather than population prevalence.

statements.quote: The target response at 3 months postinitiation was BSA 1% or less.
statements.context: BSA means body surface area. The consensus involved 25 psoriasis experts and was published online on 28 November 2016.

completion.title: FDA licenses an IL-17 inhibitor for adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.
completion.criterion: FDA grants a biologics licence to an IL-17 inhibitor for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. Achieved on 21 January 2015 with secukinumab. Its original label reports week-12 PASI90 in 145/245 patients (59%) and 175/327 patients (54%) receiving 300 mg, versus 3/248 (1%) and 5/326 (2%) receiving placebo in the two pivotal trials.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, approval letter for BLA 125504/0.
completion.threshold_quote: We have approved your BLA for COSENTYX™ (secukinumab) effective this date.
completion.basis: The licence establishes an approved treatment; its label supplies evidence that PASI90 is attainable during treatment. PASI90 is also an EDF treatment goal. FDA's efficacy endpoints were PASI75 and clear/almost-clear Investigator's Global Assessment. The observed PASI90 response proportions are evidence of clearance, rather than a numerical licensing minimum.

milestones.title: An IL-17 antibody has laboratory activity and toxicology supporting exposure in humans.
milestones.criterion: Establish intended biological activity and characterise toxicity in pharmacologically relevant species sufficiently to support human exposure under ICH S6. FDA's review records inhibition of IL-17A/TNF-induced IL-6 release in human synoviocytes (IC50 0.14 ± 0.02 nM). A 13-week subcutaneous cynomolgus study used 15, 50 and 150 mg/kg/week, with 3 animals/sex/group and 2/sex/group during recovery; the reviewer assigned a no-observed-adverse-effect level of 50 mg/kg/week. These are reported results, not universal dose or potency requirements.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, ICH S6 sections 1.2 and 3.1–3.3, retained in S6(R1). The guidance covers nonclinical work before and throughout clinical development.
milestones.threshold_quote: The objectives of the preclinical safety studies are to define pharmacological and toxicological effects

milestones.title: An IL-17A antibody improves PASI and IGA versus placebo at four weeks in adults with plaque psoriasis.
milestones.criterion: Meet the psoriasis proof-of-concept study's week-4 PASI and Investigator's Global Assessment (IGA) endpoints against placebo. Published on 6 October 2010: 36 adults received one intravenous infusion of secukinumab 3 mg/kg or placebo, 18 per group. Mean PASI fell 58% versus 4% (P = 0.0001); IGA categories improved in 15/18 versus 2/18 participants (P = 0.0004).
milestones.set_by: Novartis and participating investigators, psoriasis proof-of-concept protocol published by Hueber and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: In the psoriasis study, the co-primary endpoints were PASI and IGA at week 4.

milestones.title: An IL-17A antibody increases week-12 PASI75 responses over placebo in a dose-finding trial.
milestones.criterion: Increase the proportion achieving PASI75, at least 75% improvement from baseline, after 12 weeks versus placebo in a randomised dose-finding study. Published online on 18 January 2013: 125 adults were randomised across five groups. Secukinumab 150 mg at weeks 0, 4 and 8 produced PASI75 in 82% of 27 participants, versus 9% of 22 receiving placebo (P < 0.001).
milestones.set_by: Novartis and participating investigators, phase II dose-ranging protocol published by Papp and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary efficacy outcome was at least 75% improvement from baseline in the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index score (PASI 75)

milestones.title: An IL-17 inhibitor meets week-12 PASI75 and clear/almost-clear endpoints in two pivotal trials.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate superiority to placebo at week 12 on both PASI75 and IGA modified 2011 scores of 0 or 1, meaning clear or almost clear skin with at least a two-grade improvement. ERASURE enrolled 738 adults and FIXTURE 1,306. The FDA analysis used a graphical multiplicity procedure with family-wise error 0.05 and initial alpha 0.025 per dose. Both secukinumab doses met both endpoints in both trials (P < 0.0001). With 300 mg, IGA responses were 160/245 versus 6/248 and 202/327 versus 9/326 for placebo.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Statistical Review and Evaluation for BLA 125504/0, assessing the prespecified ERASURE and FIXTURE efficacy tests.
milestones.threshold_quote: PASI 75 response at Week 12 and IGA 0 or 1 at Week 12

milestones.title: FDA advisers conclude that an IL-17 inhibitor's benefits and risks support approval for plaque psoriasis.
milestones.criterion: The FDA Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee concludes, after weighing risks and benefits, that the data support approval of an IL-17 inhibitor for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis in adults eligible for systemic therapy or phototherapy. On 20 October 2014, the committee voted 7 yes, 0 no and 0 abstentions for secukinumab. This recommendation preceded the licensing decision.
milestones.set_by: FDA Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee, approval voting question of 20 October 2014, reproduced in FDA's Cross Discipline Team Leader Review.
milestones.threshold_quote: Considering potential risks and benefits do the available data support approval of secukinumab

not_found: No requirement that at least half of treated patients achieve PASI90 at week 12 was found in FDA's approval letter, original label or statistical review.

results.finding: Secukinumab in cynomolgus monkeys (3/sex/group): NOAEL 50 mg/kg/week.
results.detail: In a 13-week subcutaneous study, the reviewer identified immunotoxicity. Secukinumab also inhibited IL-17A/TNFα-induced IL-6 release in human synoviocytes (IC50 0.14 ± 0.02 nM). FDA found the application approvable from a pharmacology/toxicology perspective.
results.quote:
Based on evidence 
for immunotoxicity, the NOAEL was determined to be 50 mg/kg/week with an AUC0-168 hr 
= 297000 µg● hr/mL.

results.finding: In two secukinumab trials (N=738 and 1,306), both doses beat placebo on week-12 PASI75 and IGA endpoints (p<0.0001).
results.detail: The IGA endpoint required a score of 0 or 1 with at least a two-grade improvement. The protocol used a graphical procedure to control family-wise error at 0.05.
results.quote:
Both secukinumab 300 mg and 150 mg were superior to placebo at Week 12 (p<0.0001) 
for the co-primary endpoints of PASI 75 response and IGA of 0 or 1, as well as the key 
secondary endpoint of PASI 90 response at Week 12 in both Trials 2302 and 2303.

results.finding: FDA licensed secukinumab for eligible adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis on 21 January 2015; sample size not applicable.
results.detail: The approval letter does not report the pivotal trials’ PASI90 results.
results.quote: We have approved your BLA for COSENTYX™ (secukinumab) effective this date.

results.finding: Secukinumab received initial U.S. approval in 2015; 145 of 245 patients (59%) receiving 300 mg achieved PASI90 at week 12.
results.detail: The FDA label indicates secukinumab for adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. It gives the approval year, but not the exact approval date.
results.quote:
PASI 90 response at Week 12 was achieved with COSENTYX 300 mg and 150 mg compared to placebo in 59% 
(145/245) and 39% (95/245) versus 1% (3/248) of subjects, respectively (Trial 1) and 54% (175/327) and 42% (137/327) 
versus 2% (5/326) of subjects, respectively (Trial 2).
